lines.source: The Matrix: knowing versus taking a path, as an explicit narrative reading. The architecture experiment is independent of that fiction.
lines.text: In The Matrix, knowing the way and taking it are different problems. A powerful AI can also lack control over the conditions for acting.

lines.source: The Matrix Reloaded: Keymaker access and timing dependency, source register in cinema-storytelling-runbook.md. Original schematic time window, not measured robot performance.
lines.text: With the Keymaker, that gap becomes a door and a narrow window. Our machine has its own window.

lines.source: Chosen latency pattern, not a claim that every inference system lacks a timing bound.
lines.text: One answer arrives in time. The next arrives late. A fast average cannot give that moment back.

lines.source: Synthetic blocking baseline: unfinished work queues later controller jobs.
lines.text: Make the controller wait for inference. Now one late answer holds up the work behind it. Watch the queue.

lines.source: Synthetic async design: fixed controller and admission costs, bounded handoff and isolated worker assumed.
lines.text: Let the AI propose in another worker. A bounded handoff lets this controller keep moving. We have removed the waiting dependency.

lines.source: Observation age and context validity differ from result arrival time.
lines.text: But this proposal remembers a world that has moved on. Its arrival is new. Its observation is old.

lines.source: The Matrix Revolutions Mobil Ave authority boundary, as an explicit analogy. Actual model checks observation age and context version; neither establishes action safety.
lines.text: In Revolutions, Neo's power does not control the Trainman's station. Here, a proposal needs admission: check the observation's age and context before use.

lines.source: Architecture proposal: timing and freshness do not prove action safety; no plant is simulated.
lines.text: Permission is conditional. Passing those checks does not make an action safe. Action limits and the baseline need their own evidence.

lines.source: Architect account in The Matrix Reloaded, not the claim that Zion is another simulation. Structural analogy only. Actual shared stalls are authored events; neither fiction nor analogy validates the engineering claim.
lines.text: The Architect describes Zion's rebellion inside a larger cycle. Here is a smaller dependency: two separate workers still share one machine. Inference can stall control through that shared resource. Isolation and worst-case timing need separate evidence.

lines.source: Dr. Ozgur Ural's open architecture experiment. Timing is simulated; task success and proposal usefulness are not measured.
lines.text: This is my synthetic architecture experiment. Timing, useful AI input and safe action are different tests. Intelligence needs an execution contract.
